claim.why_it_matters: Table 10 is the normative precedence table a compiler consults to decide whether a PICTURE character-string is legal. The dropped mark states that a 'P' may not precede a 'P', so a PICTURE with repeated scaling P (e.g. PPP9 / 9PPP) reads as illegal from the transcription while the standard permits it - the same falsely-restrictive direction as the lost choice-indicator defects.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, by pixel measurement of the rendered page and by byte-exact reading of the source markdown.

PRINTED PAGE (E:/Temp/specrecon/v490/spec_p490.png, 300 dpi). I detected the ruled grid rather than eyeballing it. Horizontal rules at y = 450/531/633/714/796/878/959/1041/1123/1205 give the nine 'Other symbols' rows: 9, A X, S, V, P, P, 1, N, E. Vertical rules at x = 272, 358, 453/464 (the double rule after the row-label column), then 551, 614, 677, 740, 816, 892, 984, 1065, 1146, 1225, 1306, 1387, 1467, 1547, 1628, 1690, 1765, 1828, 1892, 1954, 2019, 2082, 2145, 2209 - exactly 24 data columns. Per-cell dark-pixel counts for the two rows in question:
  V  -> columns 1(131) 2(129) 5(129) 8(131) 10(129) 12(129) 14(131) 16(129) 18(129) 20(131)  = 10 marks
  P1 -> columns 1(131) 2(129) 5(129) 8(129) 10(129) 12(129) 14(131) 16(129) 18(129) 20(131)  = 10 marks
Every other cell in both rows has a dark-pixel count of exactly 0, so there is no threshold ambiguity: each count of ~129-131 is a full 'x' glyph and each blank is truly blank. The printed P row is mark-for-mark identical to the printed V row above it, exactly as claimed.

COLUMN LABELS. Table 10 spans pages 489-490; the 'First Symbol' header band is printed on p.489 only. I rendered p.489 and read it: the 24 columns are 1 'B 0 /', 2 ',', 3 '.', 4 '+', 5 '+ -', 6 '+ -', 7 'CR DB', 8 'cs', 9 'cs', 10 'Z *', 11 'Z *', 12 '+ -', 13 '+ -', 14 'cs', 15 'cs', 16 '9', 17 'A X', 18 'S', 19 'V', 20 'P', 21 'P', 22 '1', 23 'N', 24 'E'. The claim's column identification is therefore correct in every one of the ten positions, including that the tenth mark sits in column 20, the leftmost 'P' column.

MARKDOWN (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, verified in the canonical file at lines 20719-20721, not merely in the extracted work unit). Line 20719 (V) has 27 pipe-cells with 'x' at cell indices 2,3,6,9,11,13,15,17,19,21 -> data columns 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20 = 10 marks, an exact match to the print. Line 20720 (first P) has 26 pipe-cells with 'x' at indices 2,3,6,9,11,13,15,17,19 -> data columns 1,2,5,8,10,12,14,16,18 = 9 marks. The first nine align with the print with zero offset; data column 20 is empty and the remaining tail is empty. So the tenth mark was LOST, not shifted, wrapped, or relocated to an adjacent line - I checked the neighbouring rows and no stray 'x' appears there. Both quoted rows in the claim are verbatim-accurate against the source file.

RULED OUT: not page-break furniture (the loss is inside one row of one table, both rows fully on p.490); not line wrapping or hyphenation (single-line table rows); not a formatting-only difference (an 'x' at an intersection of a precedence table is the entire normative payload of the cell); not a misquote (both sides quoted exactly). The semantics is as claimed: the row is 'second symbol = P (leading-P group)' and the lost column is 'first symbol = P (leading-P group)', i.e. the cell that permits P to follow P. The print's second P row confirms the reading, carrying its own P-after-P mark in column 21, the trailing-P column. Without the column-20 mark the transcription forbids repeated leading scaling P (PIC PPP9), which the standard permits - falsely restrictive, the same direction as the lost choice-indicator defects.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, and the claim is accurate as written; two refinements worth recording.

(1) Mechanism: the markdown P row is not a row whose 'x' was blanked - it is a row that is one CELL short. It has 26 pipe-cells against the V row's 27, and the missing cell is the trailing 'x' cell itself. The nine surviving marks are still in their correct columns (no offset), so the defect is a clean loss of the column-20 'P' mark and nothing else.

(2) Collateral damage in the same block, which the claim does not mention and which should be fixed in the same repair: the SECOND P row (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 20721) is likewise 26 cells and has also lost a cell, but an EMPTY one, somewhere between columns 8 and 17. Its five marks all survive yet three of them land one column too far left: the print has that row marked at columns 5 (+ -), 8 (cs), 18 (S), 19 (V) and 21 (P, the trailing-P column), while the markdown places them at 5, 8, 17, 18 and 20. Read literally the transcription therefore also asserts that the trailing P may follow 'A X', 'S' and the LEADING P rather than 'S', 'V' and the trailing P - a second normative corruption of the same table, non-restrictive in one direction and falsely restrictive in another. Additionally the header/first row (line 20715) carries one EXTRA leading blank cell (27 cells with data starting at index 3 rather than index 2), so the Table 10 continuation block on p.490 is column-misaligned in three separate rows. The p.490 markdown also reproduces no column headers at all - the 'First Symbol' header band is transcribed only under p.489 - so the surviving marks cannot be resolved to symbols without cross-page context. Any repair should re-derive all nine rows of the p.490 block against the 24-column header on p.489 rather than patching the single missing 'x'.
